exposure: Lenalidomide (0.5, 1, 2, 4 mg/kg/day orally on gestation days 20-50)
Thalidomide (15 mg/kg/day orally on gestation days 26-28, positive control)
outcome: External fetal malformations (e.g., upper and lower extremities)
cohort: The study included groups of 5 pregnant cynomolgus monkeys for each treatment arm.
finding: Lenalidomide administration to pregnant cynomolgus monkeys resulted in dose-dependent intrauterine loss and fetal malformations, particularly limb defects, similar to the teratogenic effects observed with thalidomide, even at maternal exposures significantly lower than therapeutic doses in humans.
birth_weight: Fetal body weights were measured at gestation day 100, showing no effects from treatment.
gest_age: Fetuses were examined at gestation day 100; exposures occurred during gestation days 20-50 (lenalidomide) and 26-28 (thalidomide).
